advection_duo.accuracy: O(h) on a quasi-uniform icosahedral triangular mesh
advection_duo.reference: Heikes et al. (2023), J. Adv. Model. Earth Syst. 15:e2022MS003192 (DUO icosahedral triangular C-grid); flux-form scalar advection (transport) on the triangular primal cell — the divergence of the advective flux q·U, composing the divergence_duo stencil with a centered edge reconstruction of the transported scalar. div(U·q)_i = (1/tri_area[i]) Σ_{k=1}^{3} edge_sign_on_face[i,k] · dc_edge[e] · U[e] · (q[i] + q[cell_neighbors[i,k]])/2, with e = edges_on_face[i,k], U[e] the prescribed edge-normal mass-flux velocity (edge-located, oriented along the reference normal n̂_e so edge_sign_on_face turns it outward), and (q[i]+q[nbr])/2 the second-order centered reconstruction of q at the edge. The advective tendency is -div(U·q). Same cell-output reduction shape as divergence_duo and nn_diffusion_duo, extended to gather the transported scalar at the cell and its three edge-neighbours; the geometry coefficient s·dc/A is const-folded, only q and U reach the per-step hot tree. The reduction bound is the constant 3 (closed-icosahedral valence).
